hook.text: Six corporations control over 90% of the media Americans consume. In 1983, it was fifty.

buildup.text: Media consolidation means fewer owners decide what stories get told and which voices get amplified.

discovery.text: When one company owns the newspaper, TV station, and radio in a city, diversity of opinion shrinks.

twist.text: Tech giants added a new layer — Google and Meta now control where most advertising dollars go.

climax.text: More media channels than ever, but fewer companies controlling the pipes behind them.

punchline.text: More channels. Fewer owners. Same problem.

quiz.question: How many corporations control 90% of American media?
